elections.notes: Republican primary runoff for Governor (Toby Doeden vs. incumbent Larry Rhoden), required because no candidate received 35% in the June 2, 2026 primary; absentee voting began June 12, 2026. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.

Advance in-person voting may begin July 15 (varies by county) and must begin in all counties by July 28; it ends at 12:00 noon on August 3. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.

Registration deadline is for mail/online; in-person registration with proof of residency continues through Election Day. Secretary of State and Attorney General nominees are chosen at party conventions, not in this primary; the primary nominates for U.S. Senate, Governor, U.S. House, and the Legislature. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.

Primary nominates for all 8 U.S. House districts, State Auditor (the only statewide office up in 2026), and the Legislature; no U.S. Senate or Governor race in Missouri in 2026. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.

Virginia's 2026 primary, originally set for June 16, was moved to August 4, 2026 per an official Department of Elections news release; primaries are held only for offices/parties with contested nominations. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.

Top-two primary; ballot includes U.S. Representative, State Senator/Representative, and statewide judicial (Supreme Court, Court of Appeals) — no U.S. Senate or Governor race in 2026 and no statewide executive offices; all-mail voting with ballots mailed by July 17, so no traditional early-voting period; registration deadline is online/mail, in-person through Election Day. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
State primary (held concurrently with county general elections) nominating candidates for the Nov. 3 general. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Same-day voter registration available; all-mail election with in-person voting at voter service centers (excluding Sundays). Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.

Same-day registration is not available for primaries. The last day to register or enroll by mail was July 24, 2026; the online system closed that day at 11:59 p.m. Early voting ran Aug 3 through Aug 9. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Same-day voter registration available. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Same-day voter registration available. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Same-day voter registration available. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Top-four nonpartisan open primary; top four advance to the ranked-choice general election. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.

Closed primary; early-voting dates shown are the mandatory statewide period (counties may offer additional days). The Aug 18 primary included Republican and Democratic U.S. Senate contests. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Same-day voter registration available (register and vote at the polls); advance registration closed August 3, 2026. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Runoff applies only to races in which no candidate received a majority in the June 16, 2026 primary. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Same-day voter registration available. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Primary held on a Wednesday; RI Department of State confirms the new 2026 primary date of September 9 due to the Labor Day holiday. Historical — election already held; record retained for archive.
Closed primary; early-voting sites closed Sunday Sept. 6 and Labor Day Sept. 7 within the listed window.
General election uses ranked-choice voting among top-four primary finishers.

Statewide primary was held May 19, 2026, with runoffs in June; Alabama has no early in-person voting; Governor (Ivey term-limited) and the Class 2 U.S. Senate seat are both on the ballot. Registration closes 15 days before the election (Oct 19; per NCSL voter-registration table updated 2026-05-20, cross-checked 2026-09-28); no same-day registration.
A General Runoff Election, if required for eligible (e.g., nonpartisan/municipal) races, is set for December 1, 2026.
No U.S. Senate seat is up in Arizona in 2026; Governor and all other statewide executive offices plus all 9 U.S. House districts and the Legislature are on the ballot.
All active registered voters are mailed ballots beginning 2026-10-05; same-day (conditional) voter registration available after the deadline; no U.S. Senate seat on California's 2026 ballot.

All-mail voting state; every voter receives a mail ballot. Ballots are mailed to all registered voters Oct 2 through Oct 9, 2026; active, eligible registered voters receive one in that initial dispatch. Oct 26, 2026 is the deadline to register and still receive a mailed ballot (through the 8th day before the election). Eligible voters may register in person at a county voter service and polling center through Election Day, Nov 3. Voter service and polling centers open at least 15 days before the election (Oct 19) and run through Election Day, when they are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.; the minimum schedule excludes Sundays and the first Saturday, and local hours vary. Ballots must be in the county clerk's hands by 7 p.m. on Election Day; military and overseas ballots follow separate rules. Same-day registration is available during early voting and on Election Day.

Same-day voter registration available. The ordinary by-mail and online registration cutoff is Oct 16, 2026 (18 days before the election); same-day registration is available in person during early voting and on Election Day. Early voting hours are 10 a.m.–6 p.m. daily, extended to 8 a.m.–8 p.m. on Oct 27 and Oct 29. Any eligible registered voter may request an absentee ballot without an excuse; the deadline to request one is Nov 2, 2026. Narrow Election Day exceptions (for example, sudden illness, hospital or nursing-home patients, and overseas voters) are not shown here. Absentee ballots must be received by 8 p.m. on Nov 3 if mailed or returned by an immediate family member or designee; a voter returning the ballot in person must deliver it by Nov 2.

Same-day voter registration available. Registration closes 21 days before the election (Oct 13; per NCSL table updated 2026-05-20, cross-checked 2026-09-28); same-day registration is available during early voting and on Election Day.
Early-voting sites closed Sunday Oct. 25 within the listed window; Delaware has no 2026 governor's race (next in 2028).
Includes special U.S. Senate election for the remainder of the unexpired term (appointee Ashley Moody's seat); early-voting dates shown are the mandatory statewide period.

Governor's race is open (Kemp term-limited) and the Class 2 U.S. Senate seat is up; May 19 primary and June 16 primary runoff were held before July 25. Absentee ballot applications are due by Oct 23, 2026.

Same-day voter registration is available at voter service centers from 10 days before the election through Election Day. Early voting runs at voter service centers Oct 20 through Nov 3 (excluding Sundays), and ballots are due by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Paper registration applications: the state's table lists Oct 26, 2026, but its general rule sets 4:30 p.m. on the tenth day before the election (Oct 24); the earlier date is shown as the register-by date. Online registration is open at any time. Requests for a ballot sent to a temporary alternate mailing address are due Oct 27, 2026.

Same-day voter registration available (pre-registration deadline is 5:00 p.m. Monday, October 19, 2026); early voting shown is in-person absentee at the county auditor's office. Mail registrations must be postmarked 15 days before the election (Oct 19; per NCSL table updated 2026-05-20, cross-checked 2026-09-28); same-day registration is available during in-person absentee voting and on Election Day.

Same-day voter registration available at the polls on Election Day; early in-person voting offered only in counties that choose to conduct it. Registration closes 11 days before the election (Oct 23; per NCSL table updated 2026-05-20, cross-checked 2026-09-28); Election Day registration is available.

Open U.S. Senate seat (Sen. Dick Durbin not seeking re-election) plus Governor, all 17 U.S. House districts, statewide constitutional officers, and the General Assembly; early voting begins Sept 24 at election-authority main sites, with additional permanent sites opening later (e.g., Oct 19 in some jurisdictions). Mail registration closes 28 days before the election (Oct 6; per NCSL table updated 2026-05-20, cross-checked 2026-09-28); online registration remains open through Oct 18, with grace-period and same-day registration through Election Day.

No U.S. Senate seat and no Governor's race in Indiana in 2026; ballot includes all 9 U.S. House districts, statewide offices (Secretary of State, Auditor/Comptroller, Treasurer), and the Legislature; early (in-person absentee) voting ends at 12:00 noon on Nov 2.

U.S. Senate Class II seat (incumbent Roger Marshall) and an open Governor's race (Gov. Kelly term-limited) are both on the 2026 ballot; advance in-person voting may begin Oct 14, must begin in all counties by Oct 27, and ends at 12:00 noon Nov 2.
Early voting shown is Kentucky's three-day no-excuse in-person absentee period; state legislative seats also on the ballot (no statewide constitutional offices in 2026).

Officially titled 'U.S. Senate General/Open U.S. Representative Primary/Open Primary Election': the U.S. Senate race is the party-general round (the Senate primary was held May 16, 2026), while U.S. House and other open-primary offices hold their open (jungle) primary this day; online (GeauxVote) registration deadline is Oct 13; early voting excludes Sunday, Oct 25. Absentee ballot requests are due by 4:30 p.m. Oct 30, and a registrar must receive a voted absentee ballot by 4:30 p.m. Nov 2 (military and overseas voters are excluded from these deadlines).

Advance registration closes Oct 13, 2026: 5 p.m. for applications submitted by mail or in person at the local board of elections, and 11:59 p.m. for online registration. Same-day voter registration is available during early voting and on Election Day. Early voting runs Oct 22 through Oct 29, 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily, including weekends. Mailed or faxed absentee ballot requests must be received by Oct 27, 2026. Requests for a ballot to download and print are due Oct 30, 2026.

Same-day voter registration available; Maine's statewide primary was held June 9, 2026. Mail or third-party registration applications must be received by the voter's town or city by close of business on Oct 13, 2026, and online registration closes at 5 p.m. that day. In-person registration is available through the close of polls on Election Day, Nov 3. The last day to request an absentee ballot, or to vote absentee in the presence of the clerk, is Thursday, Oct 29. Absentee ballots must be returned to the municipal clerk by 8 p.m. on Nov 3.

Open U.S. Senate seat (Sen. Gary Peters not seeking re-election) and open Governor's race (Gov. Whitmer term-limited); registration deadline is mail/online, with in-person registration through 8 p.m. on Election Day (proof of residence is required for registrations made within 14 days of an election). Oct 24-Nov 1 is the constitutionally mandated minimum early voting period and some jurisdictions offer additional days. Mail requests for absentee ballots are due by 5 p.m. Oct 30, 2026; absentee ballot requests made in person must be submitted by 4 p.m. Nov 2, 2026.

Same-day voter registration is available at early-voting locations and polling places. Registration closes Oct 13, 2026: online at 11:59 p.m. and in-person drop-off at 5 p.m. In-person absentee voting runs Sept 18 through Nov 2, 2026 at local election offices during business hours; the last day, Monday, Nov 2, has offices open until 5 p.m. Beginning Oct 16, voters can cast their ballot into a ballot tabulator under the new early voting process. Absentee ballots returned in person must be received by local election offices by 5 p.m. on Election Day; absentee ballots returned by mail must be received by 8 p.m. on Election Day.

No U.S. Senate or Governor race in Missouri in 2026; State Auditor is the only statewide executive office on the ballot, alongside all 8 U.S. House seats and the Legislature. In-person absentee voting without an excuse runs Oct 20 through Nov 2, 2026. Mailed absentee ballot applications must be received by 5 p.m. on Oct 21, 2026.

Ballot also includes nonpartisan judicial races (Supreme Court, Court of Appeals, trial courts); no governor or legislature in 2026 (odd-year offices). Mississippi has no standard early in-person voting: in-person absentee voting is available only to voters who qualify under an absentee excuse, through Oct 31, 2026. The 2026 congressional primary was March 10, with the congressional primary runoff on April 7. Registration (in person or postmarked) closes Oct 5, 2026; no same-day registration.

No Governor race in 2026 (Montana elects its governor in presidential years). Regular voter registration closes Oct 5, 2026 at 5 p.m. Late registration begins Oct 6, 2026. Absentee ballots begin mailing Oct 9, 2026.

No 2026 governor's race; statewide contests are judicial (e.g., N.C. Supreme Court / Court of Appeals) plus all General Assembly seats; the statewide primary was held March 3, 2026. Same-day registration is available during early voting. In-person early voting runs Oct 15 through 3 p.m. Oct 31. Mailed absentee ballot requests are due by 5 p.m. Oct 20, 2026, and absentee ballots must be in the county office by 7:30 p.m. on Nov 3. Polls are open 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. on Election Day.

North Dakota does not require voter registration; no U.S. Senate or Governor race in 2026. Absentee ballots must be returned by the close of polls on Nov 3, 2026, and there is no postmark grace period.

Class II U.S. Senate seat and Governor both on the 2026 ballot; Secretary of State, Attorney General, Treasurer and Auditor also up. Mailed registrations must be postmarked by Oct 16, 2026, and online registration closes before midnight that day. In-person registration closes Oct 23 at 6 p.m. There is no ordinary Election Day registration; narrow exceptions apply (for example, for naturalized citizens). Early in-person voting runs Oct 5 through Nov 2. Applications for early-voting ballots to be mailed to a specific address must be received by Oct 23 at 6 p.m.

Same-day voter registration available. Registration deadlines vary by municipality 6-13 days before the election (per NCSL table updated 2026-05-20, cross-checked 2026-09-28); same-day registration is available on Election Day.

No governor or state legislative races in 2026 (those are odd-year elections in New Jersey); the statewide primary was held June 2, 2026. Early voting runs Oct 24 through Nov 1, 2026; hours are 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sunday.

Same-day voter registration is available during early voting and on Election Day at voting locations. Registration closes 28 days before the election (Oct 6; per NCSL table updated 2026-05-20, cross-checked 2026-09-28). Clerk's-office early voting begins Oct 6 and runs through Oct 31; expanded early voting at alternate sites begins Oct 17. The county clerk must receive absentee applications by Oct 20, 2026. Voted ballots must be received by 7 p.m. on Nov 3 at the clerk's office or a secure drop box. Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day.

Active registered voters receive mail ballots; no U.S. Senate seat on Nevada's 2026 ballot. In-person registration closes 28 days before the election (Oct 6; per NCSL table updated 2026-05-20, cross-checked 2026-09-28). Online registration is open through Nov 3, 2026. A registration completed online from Oct 20 through Nov 3 counts as same-day registration: the voter must vote in person with qualifying identification and receives no mail ballot. Same-day registration is available in person during early voting and on Election Day; the in-person same-day period varies by county (Washoe County lists Oct 20 through Nov 3). Mailed ballots must be postmarked by Nov 3 and received by 5 p.m. on Nov 7; if the postmark cannot be determined, the ballot must be received by 5 p.m. on Nov 6.

No U.S. Senate seat up in 2026; the statewide primary was held June 23, 2026. Registration forms must be received by the county board of elections by Oct 24, 2026, and a form sent by mail must also be postmarked at least 15 days before the election (Oct 19). Early voting runs Oct 24 through Nov 1, 2026; hours are set by each county. An early-mail or absentee ballot application must be received by the board of elections by Oct 24, 2026 to have the ballot mailed, or by Nov 2, 2026 to pick it up in person. A mailed ballot must be postmarked no later than Nov 3, 2026 and received by the board by Nov 10, 2026; a ballot delivered in person must reach the board of elections or a polling place before the polls close on Nov 3.

The U.S. Senate race is a SPECIAL election for the seat vacated by JD Vance and filled by appointee Jon Husted (no regular Ohio Senate seat is up in 2026); Governor's race is open (Gov. DeWine term-limited). Registration closes Oct 5, 2026; boards of elections and the Secretary of State's office are open until 9 p.m. that day. Absentee voting by mail begins Oct 6, and absentee ballot applications must be received by the board of elections by 8:30 p.m. on Oct 27. Early in-person voting runs Oct 6 through Nov 1: 8 a.m.–5 p.m. weekdays through Oct 23, 8 a.m.–4 p.m. Saturday Oct 24, 7:30 a.m.–7:30 p.m. Oct 26–30 (until 8:30 p.m. on Oct 27), 8 a.m.–4 p.m. Saturday Oct 31, and 1–5 p.m. Sunday Nov 1. Polls are open 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. on Nov 3, and absentee ballots from voters other than military and overseas voters must be received by the board of elections by 7:30 p.m. that day. Military and overseas voters' mailed ballots must be received by Nov 7 to count.

All-mail voting state; ballots are mailed to registered voters beginning Oct 14, 2026. Drop-box returns are accepted until 8 p.m. on Nov 3. Ballots postmarked by Nov 3 are accepted if received by Nov 10, 2026.

No traditional early in-person voting in PA (mail ballot application deadline is 5:00 p.m. October 27, 2026); Lieutenant Governor and state legislative seats also on the ballot. Completed mail ballots must be received by the county election office by 8 p.m. on Nov 3; a postmark by then is not sufficient.

Deadline to register to vote: Sunday, Oct 4, 2026. Deadline to apply for a mail ballot: Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026. The early voting and emergency mail ballot period runs Wednesday, Oct 14 through Monday, Nov 2, ending at 4 p.m. Mail ballots must be received by the State Board of Elections or placed in an authorized drop box by 8 p.m. on Nov 3.

Early voting runs daily 8:30 a.m.–6 p.m. from Oct 19 through Oct 31, closed Sunday Oct 25; statewide primaries were held June 9, 2026 (runoffs two weeks later); open governor's race (McMaster term-limited) and the Class 2 U.S. Senate seat are on the ballot. Registration: in person at most county offices by 5 p.m. Oct 2; by fax or email received by Oct 4; by mail postmarked by Oct 5. Absentee applications are due by 5 p.m. Oct 23, 2026. Absentee ballots must be received by the county voter registration and elections office by 7 p.m. on Nov 3. No same-day registration.
No same-day registration; registration closes Oct 19, 2026 at 5 p.m. Absentee voting, including in person, begins Sept 18, 2026 and runs until 5 p.m. on Nov 2, the day before the election.

Early voting runs Oct 14 through Oct 29, 2026. Absentee applications must be received by Oct 24, 2026; absentee voting by mail requires an eligibility category. Absentee ballots must be received by the county election commission by 7 p.m. on Nov 3.

The statewide primary was held March 3, 2026 (runoff May 26); U.S. Senate seat (Class 2) and Governor are both on the 2026 ballot. Early voting by personal appearance runs Oct 19 through Oct 30, 2026. Mail ballot applications must be received (not postmarked) by Oct 23, 2026; voting by mail requires an eligibility category.

All-mail voting state. Active registered voters are mailed ballots automatically beginning Oct 13, 2026; other voters may request a by-mail ballot by 5 p.m. on Oct 27, 2026. In-person early voting begins Oct 20, 2026; some counties open satellite sites later (Salt Lake County's begin Oct 27). Same-day voter registration is available in person on Election Day with two forms of valid ID; no Governor or U.S. Senate race in Utah in 2026.

No governor or General Assembly races in 2026 (odd-year offices); a district-level House of Delegates District 20 special election also appears on the Nov 3 ballot. Registration closes Oct 23, 2026; same-day registration with a provisional ballot is available through Election Day. In-person absentee voting runs Sept 18 through 5 p.m. Oct 31, 2026. Absentee applications must be received by 5 p.m. Oct 23, 2026. Absentee ballots returned in person must reach the local registrar by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Mailed absentee ballots must be postmarked by Election Day and received by noon on the third day after the election (Nov 6, 2026).

Same-day voter registration is available at your polling place on Election Day (Nov 3). All active and eligible registered voters are mailed general-election ballots automatically, with mailing completed by Oct 1, 2026. Return a ballot by hand to the presiding officer at the voter's polling place before the polls close at 7 p.m. on Election Day.

No U.S. Senate seat and no Governor's race in Washington in 2026; ballot has all 10 U.S. House districts, the Legislature, and statewide judicial offices; all-mail voting state (no traditional early-voting window). Online and mailed registrations must be received by Oct 26, 2026 (8 days before Election Day). In-person registration at the county auditor's office is available through Election Day, Nov 3. Ballots must be postmarked by Nov 3; ballots deposited in an official drop box must be in by 8 p.m. on Election Day.

Same-day voter registration is available at the polls on Election Day. Mail registrations must be postmarked by Oct 14, 2026, and online registration closes that day at 11:59 p.m. Registration at the municipal clerk's office or other designated location closes Oct 30 at 5 p.m. or at close of business, whichever is later. In-person absentee voting may begin Oct 20; municipalities set their own schedules, and in-person absentee applications end no later than Nov 1. Requests for absentee ballots by mail (including online, email or fax) are due by 5 p.m. on Oct 29, 2026. Absentee ballots must be delivered to the polling place or central-count location by 8 p.m. on Nov 3.

State legislative seats also on the ballot; no Governor race in 2026 (next in 2028). Absentee applications are due Oct 28, 2026. Absentee ballots hand-delivered to the clerk's office are due by Nov 2, 2026. Mailed ballots postmarked by Nov 3 are accepted if received by the canvass-convening hour on Nov 9, 2026; mailed ballots without a postmark are accepted if received by the day after the election (Nov 4, 2026). Electronic ballot return (for eligible military, overseas, and physically disabled voters) must be received by close of polls on Nov 3.

Same-day voter registration available (register and vote at the polls on Election Day). Advance registration closes Oct 19, 2026. Absentee ballots may be requested at any time before the day of the election; the last day to request one is Nov 2, 2026. In-person absentee voting runs Oct 6 through Nov 2, excluding county holidays.

Held only for Nov 3 races in which no candidate receives the required majority (Georgia requires a majority to win the general election). Registration deadlines: Oct 5, 2026 for state and local runoff races; Nov 2, 2026 for federal runoff races. Absentee ballot applications are due by Nov 20, 2026.

Listed on the official calendar as 'General/Special Runoff Election Day'; held only for races (e.g., nonpartisan judicial contests or special elections) in which no candidate wins the required majority on November 3.

Officially the 'Open General Election' — held only for races in which no candidate wins the required majority on Nov 3 (U.S. House districts without a majority winner, plus open-primary judicial/local races); online (GeauxVote) registration deadline Nov 21; early voting excludes Sunday, Nov 29.
